chunks: Al-Sakuni narrated from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon them both): that he was asked about a man who dies and has no heir and no 'asabah (agnates).
He said: 'He should bequeath his wealth wherever he wishes, among the Muslims, the poor, and the traveler (ibn al-sabil).'

key_terms.ابْنِ السَّبِيلِ: traveler (a specific category of beneficiary in Islamic law, often eligible for zakat or bequests)
key_terms.عَصَبَةَ: agnates (male relatives who inherit the residue after fixed shares are distributed)
key_terms.وَارِثَ: heir (specifically direct descendants or close relatives with fixed shares)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the estate of a man who dies with no heirs or agnates?
ai.summary: In the absence of both direct heirs (warith) and agnatic heirs (asabah), Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that the deceased retains full testamentary freedom to distribute his estate to any beneficiaries, such as Muslims, the poor, or travelers. This ruling highlights the flexibility of Islamic inheritance law when the fixed shares and residual heirs are absent, allowing the testator to prioritize charitable causes or specific individuals. The hadith underscores the principle that in the absence of statutory heirs, the will serves as the primary mechanism for estate distribution.
